subject: Planned maintenance — EastUS3 windowed driver swap and runtime curfew
messages:
From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Kelsey Park <kelsey@alphaapps.com>, ops@alphaapps.com
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 05 Dec 2026 10:12:00 -0800
Subject: Planned maintenance — EastUS3 windowed driver swap and runtime curfew

Hi Kelsey / Alpha Apps Ops team —

We have a scheduled maintenance event for EastUS3 next week and wanted to share details so you can plan. High level: a windowed driver swap across the regional serving fleet to update a low-level NIC/driver combination that improves throughput on certain batches. This will be a rolling operation (node-by-node) with a short "runtime curfew" for affected pods.

What you should expect
- Window: Sunday, 12 Dec 2026, 01:00–04:00 UTC (we will perform node-level swaps across the 3-hour window).
- Per-node impact: 4–8 minutes of warm restart while drivers swap and kernels rebind. Most requests will be routed away during node drain; a minority may hit fallback variants with slightly higher latency.
- Availability target: we expect application-visible success rate >99.9% across the window; short tail latency spikes (200–600ms extra) possible for in-flight sessions.
- KV cache: node restarts may evict per-node KV caches; we will proactively warm hot prefixes and enable light-weight prefix caching on fallback hosts to reduce downstream regen.

Mitigations we have in place
- Canary first: 2 pilot hosts in a non-production subnet for 30 minutes.
- Auto-fallback: traffic routed to compatible model variants (quantized/backoff profiles) when a node is drained.
- Rate-aware routing: we’ll throttle large-batch inference jobs briefly to prioritize low-latency interactive traffic.
- Rollback plan: immediate driver rollback artifact and re-provision snapshot; estimated recovery < 20 minutes if any regression detected.

Attachments: driver_release_notes_v2.pdf (summary + rollback steps), eastus3_windowed_mop.txt (operator playbook).

Action requested: please ack this window and share any blackout periods or business-critical workflows we should be aware of. If you prefer, we can shift to an alternate date in the same week — please let me know by EOD Monday.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference

From: Kelsey Park <kelsey@alphaapps.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 06 Dec 2026 02:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance — EastUS3 windowed driver swap and runtime curfew

Thanks for the heads up, Irene. Quick questions from our side: 
1) Will embeddings generation jobs (batched nightly jobs) be automatically queued off-region or will they be rate-limited? We typically run large embedding batches at 02:00 UTC.
2) Any expected change to tokenization or model output semantics after the driver update (we depend on deterministic outputs for a nightly job).

If you plan to throttle those batches, we can move our embedding window to 05:00 UTC to avoid interference. Otherwise a short heads-up before you hit our tenancy would be helpful.

—Kelsey
Kelsey Park
Head of Integrations, Alpha Apps

From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.ai>
To: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>, Kelsey Park <kelsey@alphaapps.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 06 Dec 2026 12:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Planned maintenance — EastUS3 windowed driver swap and runtime curfew

Hi all — quick technical clarifications / confirmation from the ops runbook side:

Thanks for flagging, Kelsey — we will not evict or cancel embedding jobs automatically. Plan is to rate-limit large batch jobs inbound to EastUS3 during the minutes a node is drained and rely on routing to non-impacted capacity or queued retries. Specifically:
- Embedding jobs: kept in queue; large batches will be signaled (429/Retry-After) and routed to dedicated batch hosts where possible. If Alpha Apps prefers, we can whitelist/blacklist by API key to proactively shift your batch traffic to a different region for the 02:00 UTC window.
- Determinism: there is no model change in this operation — only driver/NIC updates. No changes to tokenization or model weights. Deterministic outputs should be preserved.
- KV warming: we will run a prefix warm after the canary stage for hot prefixes you identify. Kelsey, if you can share 3–5 hot prefixes or representative queries we will ensure they're in the warm list.
- Canary and rollback: canary first for 30 minutes. If error rates for canary exceed thresholds (5xx rate > 0.5% sustained), we stop and run the rollback procedure. Rollback estimated <20 minutes plus drain reconciliation.

Runbook link: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/eastus3-driver-swap-runbook (internal ops doc, read-only link).

Cheers,
Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Planned maintenance — EastUS3 windowed driver swap and runtime curfew — final confirmation

Hi Kelsey / Alpha Apps Ops —

Thanks for the quick replies. Final confirmations and a couple of small updates to the plan based on internal review:

1) We will add Alpha Apps to the region-level routing whitelist so your embedding batches are routed to batch-dedicated hosts during the maintenance window unless you opt to shift the job timing. If you want us to push batches to a different region instead, reply and we’ll schedule the routing change.

2) We moved the start earlier by 30 minutes to allow a broader warmup buffer: New window — 12 Dec 2026, 00:30–03:30 UTC. The canary still starts at 00:30 UTC.

3) We committed the following SLO note for the event: customer-facing uptime target 99.9% across EastUS3 during the window; any visible regression will trigger credit review and a post-event report.

4) Attachments and links: driver_release_notes_v2.pdf (attached) contains rollback commands; eastus3_windowed_mop.txt is the operator playbook. Runbook: https://drive.redwood.ai/shared/eastus3-driver-swap-runbook. Support ticket opens as SUP-11234 and will be updated in real time.

Next steps for Alpha Apps:
- Reply to confirm whether you want (A) default whitelist to batch hosts, or (B) an explicit cross-region reroute for your 02:00 UTC embeddings.
- If you can share 3 representative hot prefixes for KV warming, send them by EOD Sunday and we’ll include them in the pre-warm step.

Thanks — we’ll keep updates flowing in this thread during the operation.

Best,
Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Site Reliability, Redwood Inference
